newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New charges for former US envoy in HK passport case.
newsitem.headline: New charges for former US envoy in HK passport case.

text.p: A former top U.S. immigration official had a fleeting taste of freedom on Friday before he was re-arrested by Hong Kong's anti-corruption police moments after an appeals court ruled he had been convicted of the wrong crime.
Jerry Stuchiner, 45, was sentenced to 40 months in jail last August after he admitted possessing false travel documents.
But the five Honduran passports he carried were blank except for an official stamp and signature. By legal definition, a travel document must include a photograph.

Three appeal court judges ruled he had been charged with the wrong offence and that his conviction was unsustainable, but officers from the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) were waiting as he stepped out of court a free man.
"He was re-arrested and charged with a new offence, and that is possessing equipment for making a false instrument," an ICAC spokeswoman told Reuters.
"They appeared to be Honduran passports and the prosecution thought that they were specially designed for making false instruments," she said.
Stuchiner was being held by the ICAC and would appear in district court on Tuesday, she said.
Stuchiner was first arrested last July by the ICAC, which was working with U.S. Justice Department officials probing a smuggling ring that took illegal migrants from Asia to the United States.

Prosecutors admitted their error last week when Stuchiner appeared in court to ask for a reduction in his prison term, leading him to change his appeal against sentence to an appeal against conviction.

Local media said Stuchiner had offered to plead guilty to a lesser charge and be sentenced immediately in order to avoid going through another trial, but the court decided it could not accept his offer due to a legal technicality.

Another senior U.S. immigration in Hong Kong, John DeBates, was sent back to the United States earlier this month for suspected corruption and abuse of authority. The ICAC is also looking into that case.
